reader_question: Who sets my electric bill, and who can change the rules behind it?
grade_line: Checked by the atlas: its pathway record on electric and utility bills, as of October 15, 2026
title: Six of the eight bodies behind an electric bill can change the rules behind it, and two, the regional grid operators and the investor-owned utility, apply them.
measure_line: The eight decision makers our systems atlas lists for “Why is my electric bill going up?”, by level and by whether each can change the rules or applies them, as of October 15, 2026
notes: A line ending in an open diamond is a line of authority, one body setting or approving another’s rules as the atlas records it: the legislature writes the laws that define the commission’s powers, and the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission approves the rule changes grid operators file. It shows who decides and carries no sign for which way the decision goes.
alt: Eight bodies behind an electric bill, by level. Six can change the rules: Congress and the Department of Health and Human Services, and the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, at the federal level; the state legislature and the state public utility commission; a city council or municipal utility board; and an electric cooperative’s board. Two apply them: PJM Interconnection and other regional grid operators, whose rule changes the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission approves, and the investor-owned utility. A line runs from the legislature to the commission, whose powers it sets.
